piv_relation.reason: relation_context statement withdraw_lacks_caller_authorization_check (e_7a7623c8e2ed_0005) and attacker_calls_withdraw_for_victim (e_7a7623c8e2ed_0008) explicitly show the missing caller-authorization check lets an attacker withdraw on behalf of a self-allowance-holding victim, bridging P and I to V.

evidence.text: The `WERC7575Vault.withdraw()` function does not implement the authorization check described in its comment. While the comment states "msg.sender must be owner OR have allowance for the shares", the function only calls `_shareToken.spendSelfAllowance(owner, shares)` which checks the owner's self-allowance, not the caller's authorization.

links.reported_relation: withdraw() omits the caller-authorization check and only spends the owner's self-allowance, so anyone can withdraw on behalf of a user who holds a self-allowance, enabling theft of that user's funds.
